RagShortTexts: Natangian residents have different rights and political choices.
Woodland, roads and posts affect local defence.

Variants.Content: Natangian households and leaders choose around livelihoods and rights. Woods and roads connect settlements and shape defence. Responses to outside dues or religious demands differ; mobilization still needs suppliers, home guards and contact.
Local woodland knowledge aids scouting but not food or support. Guarding every junction disperses people; assignments follow actual reports and village routes.
Agreements identify followers a chief can bind. Excess collection damages common supply; negotiated differences are more workable than assumed universal mobilization.
Fields, animals and kin differ among households. Joining or avoiding a levy each costs something; one choice does not disclose a person’s entire allegiance.
